title: The Sound of the Old Piano
passage:
In the corner of the assembly hall stood an old upright piano. It was used only a few times each year because the music room had newer instruments. Some keys were slightly yellow, and the wooden surface had small scratches. When the school began discussing whether to remove unused furniture, the piano was placed on the list.

Before a decision was made, a music teacher named Ms. Kato asked for one week. She knew the piano was old, but she wanted to learn whether it was truly useless. A piano technician inspected it and found that the instrument needed tuning and two small repairs. The cost was much lower than buying a new piano, though still high enough that the school needed a reason to keep it.

Ms. Kato opened the hall during lunch for three days and invited students to play. She expected only music club members, but other students came too. One boy played a song he had learned from his grandmother. A student who usually practiced on a digital keyboard said the old piano felt different because the keys responded to how strongly she pressed them. Several students simply sat and listened.

The school then learned something unexpected. A former student visiting for a sports event recognized the piano. He remembered using it in a graduation ceremony twenty-five years earlier. He sent a message to classmates, and several replied with similar memories. The piano was not valuable because it was rare or expensive. It was valuable because many people connected it with events in the school's history.

The school decided to repair and keep it, but not as a museum object. Students were encouraged to use it during lunch and small events. The decision did not mean every old object should be saved. Storage space and repair costs still mattered. Yet the piano taught the school to ask one more question before throwing something away: not only ‘Do we use this now?’ but also ‘Could this still have a useful or meaningful role?’ Sometimes an old object can continue by finding a new purpose.
translation:
講堂の隅に古いアップライトピアノがありました。音楽室には新しい楽器があるため年に数回しか使われず、鍵盤は少し黄ばみ、木部にも傷がありました。学校が使われていない家具の整理を始めたとき、処分候補に入りました。

決定前に加藤先生が一週間待ってほしいと頼みました。本当に使えないのか確かめたかったのです。調律師が調べると、調律と二か所の小修理で使えることが分かりました。新品よりはるかに安いものの、修理費を出すには残す理由が必要でした。

先生は三日間、昼休みに講堂を開き、自由に弾いてよいことにしました。音楽部だけでなく、祖母から教わった曲を弾く男子生徒や、普段デジタル鍵盤を使う生徒も来ました。古いピアノは押す強さで鍵盤の反応が変わると感じたそうです。弾かずに聞くだけの生徒もいました。

さらに、スポーツ行事で来校した卒業生がピアノに気づき、二十五年前の卒業式で使ったことを覚えていました。同級生へ知らせると、同じような思い出がいくつも返ってきました。珍しい高価な楽器だから価値があるのではなく、多くの人が学校の出来事と結び付けていたのです。

学校は修理して残すことにしましたが、展示物にはせず、昼休みや小さな行事で使えるようにしました。すべての古い物を保存すべきだという意味ではありません。場所や費用も重要です。ただし捨てる前に『今使っているか』だけでなく、『これから別の役割を持てるか』も考える価値があると学びました。古い物でも、新しい役割を見つければ続いていけることがあります。
